packageRules.description: Disable dependency dashboard approval for all packages

Every update is a deps(deps) commit, the type consumers' release-please configs show as Dependencies. config:best-practices pulls in :semanticPrefixFixDepsChoreOthers, whose packageRules override the top-level semanticCommitType and type most updates chore, which consumers hide. The .github/ rule below narrows this to ci for CI-only files.
Group all minor and patch updates for GitHub Actions outside .github/, such as the action.yml of a published action. Updates under .github/ are taken over by the CI rules below.

terrace-config and terrace-legal: one PR for every update of either, whatever its type. Cargo git dependencies on GitHub resolve to packageName `TimSchoenle/<repo>` (older Renovate: the full git URL), never to the crate name, and JitPack publishes the Java modules under `com.github.TimSchoenle.<repo>`.

Cargo git dependencies pinned to a monorepo release tag such as `csp-shell-v0.2.0` (release-please's `<component>-v<version>` form). The cargo manager looks these up as git/GitHub tags but keeps cargo versioning, which cannot parse the component prefix, so the lookup fails with `Can't find version matching`. Regex versioning parses the version behind the prefix and makes the prefix the compatibility, so `csp-shell-v*` only ever moves to another `csp-shell-v*` tag and never to a sibling component's tag from the same repository.

Everything under .github/ is CI and never ships: commit it as ci(deps), a type release-please hides, so a CI update never cuts a release. Matches by file rather than manager, which covers the github-actions manager, the regex manager for TimSchoenle/actions pins and customManagers:githubActionsVersions alike. separateMinorPatch: false lives here because Renovate refuses it next to matchUpdateTypes; it keeps patch and minor updates on one branch instead of a patch- prefixed second one.
One PR for every non-major CI update, across all managers. Majors stay outside the group so they arrive alone and are not auto-merged.
